Package common.hardware.motorcontroller

Class NAR_Motor

java.lang.Object
common.hardware.motorcontroller.NAR_Motor
All Implemented Interfaces:
AutoCloseable
Direct Known Subclasses:
NAR_CANSpark, NAR_TalonFX
public abstract class NAR_Motor extends Object implements AutoCloseable
One motor and its motor controller, whatever the brand. NAR_TalonFX and NAR_CANSpark fill in the details for CTRE and REV hardware, so the rest of the code can treat every motor the same way.

Units

A motor's encoder counts rotations of the motor. NAR_Motor.MotorConfig converts those into units that make sense for the mechanism, like meters or degrees, so getPosition(), getVelocity() and set(double, Control) all use your units.

Settings

Settings like current limits come in two versions: setStatorLimit sends the change to the motor controller right away, and setStatorLimitNoApply only stores it, so that configMotor(MotorConfig) can send all of them at once with apply().

Repeated commands

set(double, Control, double) skips a command identical to the last one, so calling it every loop with the same setpoint doesn't flood the CAN bus.
Since:
2023 Charged Up

    • enableSim

      public void enableSim(MotorSimModel model)
      Attaches physics so this motor moves in simulation. Does nothing on the real robot. Only attach to the leader when several motors drive one mechanism, and give the model a DCMotor for all of them, e.g. DCMotor.getKrakenX60(2).
      Parameters:
      model - The physics of what this motor drives

    • disableSim

      protected void disableSim()
      Stops simulating this motor, e.g. when it's closed.

    • updateSimulation

      public static void updateSimulation(double dtSeconds)
      Steps the physics of every motor with enableSim(MotorSimModel). Call once per loop from Robot.simulationPeriodic().
      Parameters:
      dtSeconds - Time since the last call, normally 0.02

    • configClosedLoop

      public void configClosedLoop(PIDFFConfig gains, NAR_Motor.Control mode)
      Loads PID and feedforward gains for the motor controller's own control loop, converting them from this motor's units (set by NAR_Motor.MotorConfig) to the motor controller's units. kG is applied as a constant, e.g. for an elevator.
      Parameters:
      gains - kP, kI and kD in volts per unit of position or velocity error, with time in seconds; kS and kG in volts; kV in volts per unit of velocity
      mode - NAR_Motor.Control.Position or NAR_Motor.Control.Velocity

    • configArmClosedLoop

      public void configArmClosedLoop(PIDFFConfig gains, double motorRotationsPerArmRotation)
      Like configClosedLoop(PIDFFConfig, Control) for position control of an arm, where kG is multiplied by the cosine of the arm's angle. Position 0 must be the arm held horizontal.
      Parameters:
      gains - PID and feedforward gains, as in configClosedLoop(PIDFFConfig, Control)
      motorRotationsPerArmRotation - Rotations of this motor's encoder per arm rotation: the gearing, or 1 for an absolute encoder on the arm's shaft

    • followOnController

      public boolean followOnController(NAR_Motor leader, boolean opposeLeader)
      Makes this motor copy leader's output on the motor controller itself, so it follows instantly instead of waiting for robot code.
      Parameters:
      leader - The motor to follow

      Returns:
      False if the two motor controllers can't follow each other, e.g. a Spark and a TalonFX

    • enableContinuousInput

      public void enableContinuousInput(double minInput, double maxInput)
      Treats minInput and maxInput as the same point, like 0 and 360 degrees, for something that can spin all the way around. Positions are then read within that range, and position setpoints take the shortest way around.
      Parameters:
      minInput - One end of the range, e.g. 0
      maxInput - The other end, e.g. 360

    • setMotorRotationsPerSensorRotation

      public void setMotorRotationsPerSensorRotation(double ratio)
      For an encoder that isn't on the motor, e.g. an absolute encoder on an arm's shaft: how many times the motor turns per turn of the encoder. Simulation needs this to turn the motor's motion into encoder readings. Call it before building the mechanism. 1 by default.
